meaning:
πλήρης, -ες
[in LXX chiefly for מָלֵא ;]
1. full, filled: Mat.14:20 15:37; with genitive of thing(s), Mrk.8:19; λέπρας, Luk.5:12; metaphorically, of the soul: πνεύματος ἀγίου, Luk.4:1, Act.6:3 7:55 11:24; πίστεως, Act.6:5; χάριτος, ib. Act.6:8; χ. καὶ ἀληθείας (where π. is indecl.; see M, Pr., 50; Milligan, NTD, 65, with reff. in each), Jhn.1:14; δόλου, Act.13:10; θυμοῦ, Act.19:28; ἔργων ἀγαθῶν, Act.9:36.
2. full, complete: μισθός, II Jn 8; σῖτος (π. prob. in­decl. here; see on Jhn.1:14, supr.), Mrk.4:28.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: They all ate, and were filled. They took up twelve baskets full of that which remained left over from the broken pieces.
For the earth bears fruit: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear.
Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan, and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness
The Word became flesh, and lived among us. We saw his glory, such glory as of the one and only Son of the Father, full of grace and truth.
Therefore select from among you, brothers, seven men of good report, full of the Holy Spirit and of wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business.
Watch yourselves, that we don’t lose the things which we have accomplished, but that we receive a full reward.
